newsitem.title: USA: Winds close Yosemite park, stranding visitors.
newsitem.headline: Winds close Yosemite park, stranding visitors.

text.p: All of the roads leading into California's Yosemite National Park were closed Wednesday because of high winds, stranding hundreds of visitors, park officials said.
The high winds knocked down trees and tree limbs, causing scattered power outages and a house fire.

The conditions forced the temporary closure of the three highways into the park, stranding hundreds of travelers for hours in the Yosemite Valley area, where most park lodges and campgrounds are located.
"They were trapped in and visitors were kept out," said Al Nash, a park spokesman. "Nature just keeps reminding us who is in charge."

Yosemite officials said Wednesday night they were slowly beginning to reopen some roads in areas where conditions had improved. Nash said park officials did not know the speed of the winds, but he described road conditions as "dangerous."
Flooding in early January washed away roads and damaged cabins and campsites in Yosemite Valley, forcing its closure for more than two months. The valley reopened on March 14.

The 760,000-acre (307,000-hectare) park, 150 miles (240 km) southeast of San Francisco, is visited by more than four million hikers, climbers and sightseers each year, drawn by its towering mountains, high waterfalls and scenic wilderness.
